The comparator has no build-identity precondition. requireI0Export() asserts only that the BEFORE directory exists, never that it is the pre-migration revision, so pointing LERO_I0_EXPORT_DIR at a copy of the current tree would produce 112 trivially identical cells and PASS. The reviewer closed the AFTER half from outside the artifact (storybook-static contains zero --color-overlay, and the compiled LightboxView chunk carries var(--overlay-foreground) 10%) and the owner confirmed the BEFORE export still contains --color-overlay, so the recorded result stands — this is hardening, not a refutation. Suggested fix: assert BEFORE's bundle contains var(--color-overlay and AFTER's contains zero, and fail closed otherwise. That is the check that would catch comparing a build to itself.

Invariant 1 of the rewritten 692 gate asserts two things — that each name is declared exactly once in the whole file, and that the one declaration lives inside :root — but only the first has a plant. The uncovered regression is a declaration relocated out of :root while the total count stays 1 (back into @theme inline, or into .dark): the existing plant is silent on it and only the untested arm catches it. extractBlock is never exercised against any fixture, so if it ever returned the whole file the second assertion would silently degrade into a duplicate of the first. AC5's wording is 'a planted violation of each invariant it asserts'. Fix is roughly four lines: a fixture with --overlay declared once inside @theme inline and a :root block that does not contain it, asserting the :root-scoped count is 0.

The three planted specs assert on the counting helpers rather than on the invariant bodies. Each asserts the helper's return value and mirrors the real expectation with .not.toBe(...), which is a reasonable proxy and matches the precedent this repo already uses, but it means loosening a real-tree assertion — .toBe(1) to .toBeGreaterThan(0), say — would leave all three plants green. The executor documented the choice in §7 of the session log rather than hiding it. Stronger form, if the owner wants it: run the invariant body over the planted fixture and assert it throws.

Invariant 3 makes the unit suite depend on a built .next. It throws when .next/static/css is absent, which is correctly fail-closed, but npx vitest run now hard-fails in any environment that has not built — a fresh clone, or a CI job that runs tests before the build. It also passes against a stale build, since nothing checks freshness. Worth deciding whether a bundle assertion belongs in vitest or in a separate check: script that already sequences after the build.
